title: Power Set and Counting Subsets
quickIdea: Each element is either in or out, so an n-element set has 2 to the n subsets. Applied to a Cartesian product, the same rule counts relations.
remember: The power set of S is the set of all subsets of S, written P(S).
If S has n elements then P(S) has 2 to the n elements, because each element makes one independent in-or-out decision.
The empty set has one subset (itself) and the set {empty} has two, so P(empty) = {empty} and P({empty}) = {empty, {empty}}.
Subsets of a fixed size k are counted by C(n, k), so the sizes of the parts of P(S) add up to 2 to the n.
If A has m elements and B has n, then A x B has m n elements and P(A x B) has 2 to the (m n) elements.
Because a relation from A to B is a subset of A x B, the number of relations from A to B is exactly the cardinality of P(A x B).
The number of relations on an n-element set is 2 to the (n squared), which is the count GATE asks for most often.
P(S) always has more elements than S, for finite S, because 2 to the n is greater than n.
A subset of a subset is a subset: if X subset Y and Y subset S then X is an element of P(S).

example.prompt: S = {0, 1, 2, ..., 10}. Find the cardinality of P(S), and the number of subsets of S with exactly 3 elements.
example.work: S has 11 elements (0 through 10 inclusive), so P(S) has 2 to the 11 elements. The subsets of size 3 are counted by C(11, 3) = 165.
example.answer: P(S) has 2048 elements, and 165 of them are subsets of size 3.

gateAngle: GATE CS 2015 Set 2 Q.18 is the plain cardinality of a power set (2048), and GATE CS 1993 Q.8.4 asks for the power set of A x A, which is 2 to the (n squared) - the same number as the relations on A.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 2015 Set 2 Q.18 in the linked PYQs: the cardinality of the power set of {0, 1, 2, ..., 10}.
variations.why: The set has 11 elements, and 2 to the 11 is 2048. The same rule applied to a product gives 2 to the (n squared) for the power set of A x A, which GATE CS 1993 Q.8.4 asks for and the relations card carries.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A is a set with 4 elements. How many elements does P(P(A)) have, and how many subsets of A have odd cardinality?
variations.answer: P(P(A)) has 2 to the 16 = 65536 elements, and 8 subsets of A have odd cardinality.
variations.why: P(A) has 16 elements, so P(P(A)) has 2 to the 16. Exactly half of the 16 subsets of a 4-element set have odd size: sizes 1 and 3 contribute 4 + 4 = 8.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many subsets of a 6-element set have cardinality at most 2?
variations.why: Sizes 0, 1 and 2 contribute C(6,0) + C(6,1) + C(6,2). GATE likes to add a condition on the size rather than ask for all subsets.

trap.what: Writing 2 to the n as the number of subsets of A x B, or forgetting that the power set counts subsets and not ordered pairs.
trap.why: The exponent is the number of elements of the set whose power set is taken. For A x B that is m n, not m + n, and for A x A it is n squared.
trap.counterexample: A = {1, 2}, B = {a, b, c}. A x B has 6 elements, so P(A x B) has 64 elements. Using 2 to the (2 + 3) = 32 is wrong, and 32 is not even the count of relations from A to B.

check.question: A and B are sets with 3 and 5 elements. How many relations are there from A to B?
check.explanation: A relation from A to B is a subset of A x B, which has 3 times 5 = 15 elements, so there are 2 to the 15 such subsets.
